number.why: The reported rate ratio is 0.80 (95% CI, 0.60-1.06) for total heart-failure hospitalizations with ferric carboxymaltose versus placebo through follow-up. This confirms the served IRR numbers, not the conflicting RR/HR labels. The supplied sources do not explicitly establish an intention-to-treat analysis set.

quotes.span: The second primary outcome (total heart failure hospitalizations) occurred 264 times in the ferric carboxymaltose group vs 320 times in the placebo group (rate ratio, 0.80 [95% CI, 0.60-1.06]; P = .12).
All end point events were measured through follow-up.

entry.why: The registry explicitly requires chronic HFrEF and confirmed iron deficiency and limits eligibility to adults. The question specifies no numerical EF cutoff. Downgrading to PARTLY imposes an unstated cutoff despite the source's explicit HFrEF entry criterion. The registry's <45% and publication's ≤45% should remain disclosed.

quotes.span: Inclusion Criteria: 1. Patients with chronic HFrEF (CHF) of at least 3 months duration and a history of documented LVEF\<45%. 2. Confirmed presence of ID (ferritin \< 100 ng/mL or ferritin 100 - 299 ng/mL with TSAT \< 20 %)
ELIGIBILITY AGE/SEX: minimum age 18 Years | maximum age None | sex ALL
This multicenter, randomized clinical trial enrolled 1105 patients with heart failure (defined as having a left ventricular ejection fraction of ≤45%) and iron deficiency

Administration of ferric carboxymaltose (n = 558) initially given at an intravenous dose of up to 2000 mg that was followed by 500 mg every 4 months (unless stopping criteria were met) vs a saline placebo (n = 547).

missed: The registry's explicit HFrEF and adult eligibility criteria change the entry ruling, as quoted above. Also, the claimed full-text verification is overstated: cache/iv-iron-hfref-hosp/ft_40159390.txt states, "The publisher of this article does not allow downloading of the full text in XML form." The estimate is supported by the supplied abstract; this provenance correction does not change the numerical verdict.
